newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine November car output seen up eight pct. [CORRECTED 20:43 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Argentine November car output seen up eight pct. [CORRECTED 20:43 GMT]

text.p: Argentine car production may have risen about eight percent in November as local automakers continued to try to make up for output declines in last year's recessive economy.

Most leading companies that together account for virtually the whole domestic production told Reuters they will increase output in November (corrects from "this month"). In October production had already risen to 32,000 vehicles, a 14.2 percent rise over September.
The Argentine Automakers Association (ADEFA) is expected to release its monthly production report later this week.

Ford Argentina plans a strong increase of about 20 percent to some 5,800 vehicles from 4,531 in October, a company source said. That should represent more than half of the 2,300 additional units in the whole sector expected for November.
The local unit of Volkswagen, ranked first in October with 8,094 vehicles, expects about 8,500 in November, a company official said in an interview.

CIADEA, licensee of Renault, plans to raise output to about 7,000 vehicles from 6,616 and Sevel, which makes Peugeots, sees production rising to 5,735 units from 5,654. Fiat will also increase output to 4,850 from 4,459.
Bucking the trend, General Motors acknowledged its output will likely decline to 1,600 vehicles in November from 1,859 in October.

Argentine car industry grew steadily under government protection from 100,000 cars in 1990 to a record of more than 400,000 in 1994. But it slowed to 285,000 last year in the middle of a recession unleashed by the Mexican peso devaluation at the end of 1994.

Now analysts expect seven percent economic growth in the fourth quarter, year on year, to boost GDP by 3.0 percent in 1996 as a whole. In October, domestic industrial production rose about 12 percent.
